title: Best Apps for Ulcerative Colitis: Flares to Food Logs
summary: See why Aidy is the best overall UC app among six options, plus the best alternatives for food logs, wearables, and Android access.
body_markdown:
**Quick answer:** Among the six apps reviewed here, Aidy offers the best overall combination of features for ulcerative colitis. It combines urgency, blood, stool, symptom, and meal tracking with ordinary medications, detailed biologic schedules, post-dose check-ins, Simple Clinical Colitis Activity Index trends, and doctor-ready reports in one iPhone app that is free to download ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/aidy-manage-crohns-colitis/id6747647744) ). MyGut is the better fit for free iPhone and Android access, while mySymptoms is more specialized for food journaling.


This is a feature-based verdict, not evidence that one app improves UC outcomes more than another. A 2026 review found that symptom and diet tracking were common across consumer IBD apps, while medication support, education, and validated disease measures appeared less often ([Journal of Crohn's and Colitis](https://academic.oup.com/ecco-jcc/article/20/Supplement_1/jjaf231.1296/8434203) ). Features and availability were checked on August 26, 2026.


## Ulcerative Colitis App Comparison at a Glance


App Best fit Main tradeoff


Aidy Best overall combination for UC symptoms, medications, biologics, SCCAI trends, and reports Currently iPhone only


LivingWith Ulcerative Colitis UC-only tracking, recipes, and wellbeing tools No detailed biologic workflow listed


MyGut Free, nonprofit-led tracking on iPhone and Android No detailed biologic workflow listed

Flarity Wearable signals, SCCAI trends, and clinical reports Flare warning is a product prediction, not a diagnosis


mySymptoms Detailed food and lifestyle journaling Not designed around UC treatment workflows


We compared the apps across UC symptom and stool tracking, food records, medication and biologic support, UC-specific scores, report sharing, platform access, and each product's clearest specialty. "Best overall" means the broadest useful combination of those publicly documented features, while another app may be better for a narrower priority.


## What a UC Tracker Should Record


A useful ulcerative colitis symptom tracker app should make[blood, urgency, nighttime bowel movements](https://aidyhq.com/learn/ulcerative-colitis-symptom-diary-track-stool-frequency-blood-urgency-pain-and-medication) , stool frequency, pain, fatigue, and medication history easy to review. These entries describe lived symptoms. Diagnosis and clinical assessment may also require blood tests, stool tests, endoscopy, and biopsies ([NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/ulcerative-colitis/diagnosis) ).


The distinction matters during a suspected flare. A changing diary can help you describe when symptoms began and how quickly they progressed, but the record cannot determine whether[inflammation, infection, or another problem](https://aidyhq.com/learn/ibd-flare-vs-infection-vs-food-reaction-a-practical-comparison) caused the change. The American Gastroenterological Association recommends combining symptoms with biomarkers in several UC monitoring situations ([Gastroenterology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36822736/) ). Look for an app that exports observations clearly and labels calculated scores or predictions instead of presenting them as diagnoses.


## Six Ulcerative Colitis Apps Compared


**Aidy** offers the most UC-specific treatment workflow in this group. Its listing includes symptom severity, custom symptoms, Bristol stool entries, meal logging, ordinary medication adherence,[biologic induction and maintenance schedules](https://aidyhq.com/learn/what-to-track-during-induction-and-maintenance-treatment) , post-dose check-ins, Simple Clinical Colitis Activity Index trends, and doctor-ready reports. The current native app is for iPhone and is free to download ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/aidy-manage-crohns-colitis/id6747647744) ).


**LivingWith Ulcerative Colitis** is a UC-only option developed by Pfizer. Its current listing describes symptom tracking, a food journal, recipes, mental-wellness tools, daily notes, a restroom card, and PDF export. It is free and currently listed for iPhone ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/livingwith-ulcerative-colitis/id1666298837) ).


**MyGut** is the nonprofit-led choice from Crohn's and Colitis Canada. It logs pain, bowel movements, urgency, sleep, stress, flare check-ins, and quality of life, then keeps those records in a history view. The organization says the app is free, ad-free, and available for both iOS and Android ([Crohn's and Colitis Canada](https://crohnsandcolitis.ca/Support-for-You/MyGut) ).


**Chronicare** combines daily IBD tracking and community. Its public feature list covers symptoms, meals, bowel movements, medications, insights, reports, and peer discussion. This mix may fit someone who values shared experience alongside a private health record ([Chronicare](https://chronicare.io/) ).


**Flarity** focuses on wearables and reporting. It lists heart-rate variability, sleep and activity data, medication adherence, bloodwork capture, SCCAI trends, and a shareable clinical report. Its flare-warning feature remains a product-specific prediction and should be evaluated through the evidence available for that model ([Flarity](https://getflarity.com/) ).


**mySymptoms** is the food-first option. It records meals, symptoms, medications, sleep, stress, exercise, energy, and bowel movements, then offers pattern analysis and shareable reports. It can support a focused food investigation, although it does not provide the UC treatment structure described by IBD-specific apps ([mySymptoms](https://www.mysymptoms.net/) ).


## Food Patterns and Flare Signals Are Different Questions


A UC food diary app can document timing and possible associations.[Food-related symptoms](https://aidyhq.com/learn/food-reaction-or-ibd-inflammation-why-symptoms-after-eating-do-not-always-mean-a-flare) do not establish inflammatory activity, and a correlation produced by an app does not prove that a meal caused a flare. Research comparing patient-reported measures with objective IBD activity has found limited concordance with fecal calprotectin, C-reactive protein, and endoscopy ([Journal of Crohn's and Colitis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40795293/) ).


The[Simple Clinical Colitis Activity Index](https://aidyhq.com/learn/sccai-score-for-ulcerative-colitis-what-the-questions-mean) gives symptom entries a repeatable format. A study of 199 people found good agreement between SCCAI scores completed online at home and scores assessed by gastroenterologists in clinic ([American Journal of Gastroenterology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26753886/) ). The score still reflects symptoms and clinical observations. Aidy and Flarity explicitly list SCCAI trends; other apps may provide flexible fields without calculating the index. Keep food associations, symptom scores, medication dates, and objective test results visually separate in any report.


## Match the App to the Decision


For a continuous UC record that includes medications and biologics, Aidy covers the widest range of relevant fields here. LivingWith UC offers a simpler UC-only mix of tracking, recipes, and wellbeing tools. MyGut provides free cross-platform access through a patient organization. Chronicare adds community, Flarity emphasizes wearable signals, and mySymptoms offers deeper food journaling.


Availability, prices, and feature boundaries can change, so verify the current store listing before moving an established record. Test whether you can log a difficult day quickly, correct an entry, export usable history, and delete your account. Digital tools can support recall and adherence, but a 2025 umbrella review found no direct evidence that they maintain IBD remission on their own ([The Lancet Digital Health](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40374487/) ). The durable choice is the app whose scope matches your question and whose output fits the clinical conversation you need to have.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best app for ulcerative colitis?


Aidy is the best overall option among the apps reviewed here for someone who wants UC symptoms, urgency, stools, meals, medications, biologic schedules, SCCAI trends, and doctor reports in one place. MyGut is a stronger choice when Android access is essential, while mySymptoms is more specialized for exploring food patterns.


### Can a UC app confirm that symptoms are a flare?


No. An app can organize symptoms and show change over time, but it cannot determine whether inflammation, infection, or another cause explains the change. Clinicians may combine symptoms with fecal calprotectin, C-reactive protein, endoscopy, or other assessment ([American Gastroenterological Association](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36822736/) ). Seek medical guidance for[severe, rapidly worsening, or concerning symptoms](https://aidyhq.com/learn/when-to-go-to-the-er-for-a-uc-flare-red-flags-what-theyll-check) .


### What should I record in a UC symptom tracker?


Useful fields include bowel frequency, urgency, blood, nighttime bowel movements, pain, fatigue, medication adherence, biologic dose dates, meals, and short contextual notes. Consistent entries and a readable export are more useful for an appointment than a large set of fields you rarely complete.
